description: The bar chart illustrates the performance ratio (in percentage) of three large language models—Llama3 (blue), ChatGPT (yellow), and an unnamed model represented by red bars—across three distinct domains: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. The vertical axis, labeled “Ratio (%)”, ranges from 50 to 90 with tick marks at 10-unit intervals, indicating the evaluation metric for each model’s performance in that category. The horizontal axis categorizes the domains. In the “Movies” category, Llama3 and the red model both achieve approximately 90%, while ChatGPT scores around 73%. In “Songs”, Llama3 scores about 84%, the red model again reaches 90%, and ChatGPT drops to roughly 62%. In “Basketball”, Llama3 scores approximately 67%, the red model falls to about 57%, and ChatGPT scores around 61%. The chart visually suggests that the red model performs best in Movies and Songs, while Llama3 leads in Basketball; ChatGPT consistently underperforms relative to the other two models across all categories. The legend at the top identifies the color coding for each model, and the bars are grouped by category, allowing direct comparison within each domain. No error bars or statistical annotations are present, and the chart does not indicate whether the ratios represent accuracy, recall, or another metric. The title of the associated paper, “How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception,” implies that the chart may be used to demonstrate how model performance varies with the popularity or cultural salience of knowledge domains, though this interpretation is not explicitly labeled in the chart itself.
